title: 401 refresh handling can recurse on the refresh endpoint and stampede concurrent requests
reasoning: The response interceptor handles every 401 by calling api.post('/refresh-token') through the same axios instance. A 401 from /refresh-token therefore enters the same interceptor with a fresh request config whose _retry flag is unset, so persistent refresh-token 401s can recursively issue more refresh requests instead of immediately clearing auth and redirecting as the test expects. The same block also has no shared in-flight refresh promise or queue, so simultaneous 401s each initiate their own refresh despite the concurrent-401 test documenting the intended single-refresh behavior.
reproduction: Configure /protected to return 401 and /refresh-token to always return 401; the refresh request is intercepted as another refreshable 401. Separately, fire three protected requests concurrently with an expired token and observe three /refresh-token calls instead of one.
recommendation: Bypass refresh logic for the refresh endpoint itself and reject/clear auth immediately when it returns 401. Add a module-level refresh promise or request queue so concurrent 401s await one refresh and then retry with the resulting token.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The refresh-failure test only uses replyOnce for /refresh-token, which lets subsequent mock behavior terminate the recursion rather than proving persistent 401 handling. The concurrent test asserts only that localStorage eventually has the refreshed token and explicitly avoids asserting the refresh call count.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test where /refresh-token always returns 401 and assert exactly one refresh attempt, token removal, and /login redirect. Add a concurrent 401 test that asserts mock.history.post filtered to /refresh-token has length 1.
minimumFixScope: Update app/api.ts response interceptor refresh handling and strengthen app/__tests__/api.test.ts around refresh endpoint 401s and concurrent refresh count.
